If one were trying to get to Switzerland from Dallas - how would you recommend getting there? Flights from Dallas to Zurich are so expensive and also just LONG? Has anyone flown to germany or italy instead and then gotten to Zurich? Would love some ideas!
Dallas to Amsterdam seems great - but don't see an easy way to get to Zurich or Interlaken? We are a family of 4 (2 adults and 2 children)

Set up price alerts on Google flights. Select different destinations and change the dates by a few days. Google Flights is a great resource, you can see the prices for the entire month, as often changing dates by a few days can reduce the price significantly. Use this as a research tool. Always buy flights directly from the airlines.
That being said , prices are higher, and you will need to be diligent , checking often, to find acceptable prices. If you have a lot of time, open an airlines credit card to receive bonus sign up points and discounts.
Good luck!

You are going to have a connection somewhere to fly to Zurich from Dallas (DFW).
I assume this is a summer trip since you have 2 children, s presumably school-age.
I see lots of flights on the British Airways website, using a combination of American Airlines, Iberia, and/or
British Airways, that have an overall flight time of 14-16 hours, which is not bad at all.
The connection airport will be Madrid if you have Iberia in the mix;
otherwise it will be at Heathrow.
Price for any of them is around $1400 roundtrip;
that is pretty much what people are seeing for summer 2024 travel.
But as noted above, prices can vary day to day, so if you are flexible by a day or three, that may help with a slightly lower price.
A direct flight to Amsterdam only makes sense if (a) you want to spend time in Amsterdam, (b) you want to spend time in Germany, and (c) you are OK spending time and money on trains.
The train trip between Amsterdam and
Zurich or Interlaken is around 9-10 hours at best, so you need to break that up with at least one overnight on the way.
The simplest route I can see is via Frankfurt and Basel, but there are other options.
We actually did this ourselves on our way to Switzerland in 2018,
but we wanted to visit friends in Amsterdam, and we had several extra days to spend on our way from there to Mürren.
So we made overnight stops in Bamberg (which was out of the way) ;and Basel.
I doubt that would work for your family’s vacation in Switzerland.
But if there is a direct flight to Amsterdam from your airport, you could certainly take that flight on your way to Zurich (or Geneva).
That is, make Amsterdam your connecting airport in Europe.
Fly to a major airport on the East Coast, either connect that day or spend the night.
If you follow Phred’s advice make sure your flights are all on one ticket.
You should not fly to a US airport and then have a separate ticket to Europe the same day.
Too risky.
And spending the night will just add expense unless you have friends to stay with for free.

Reviews of Best Family Friendly Hotels of Dallas Texas
Cowboy Bars are part of the Wild West scene in family-friendly Dallas.A family suite at Dallas' Highland Hotel on Mockingbird Lane.The Dallas Aloft has a Re:mix Lounge with a pool table for guests.The Mansion on Turtle Creek is one of Dallas' most historic properties.
The FTF Staff reviews the most family-friendly, comfortable hotels in Dallas, Texas, where budgets range from fancy enough for the TV show “Dallas” to funky drive-by motels. Since the city is so spread out and DART public transit is limited, you might want to choose your hotel based on its location.
### Dallas Hotels in Downtown
Omni Dallas Hotel555 S. LamarDallas, Texas 75202214/744-6664Rates: $-$$This startlingly modern hotel rises from the Convention Center boasting sparkling glass, steel, Texas artwork, and impressive environmentally-efficient standards for lighting, maintenance and room design. A beautiful exterior pool deck, enormous infinity pool spilling over the skyline and sauna will appeal to kids as much as the lobby coffee shop that puts out “samples” of the day’s muffins, chocolates and pastries for guests to nibble on. There’s lots of fine dining, whether you’re into a big Texas steak or the lighter farm-to-market fare at Texas Spice. Teens and up will enjoy the Owner’s Box, a state-of-the-art interactive sports bar with a 16-foot screen among dozens of others. The hotel has many seasonal and weekend discounts, making it a good value most of the year. In addition to 1,000 comfortable spacious rooms — this place is really big — families with younger children will appreciate the Omni Sensational Kids program which provides loaner toys inside suitcases filled with games and books, gives out an activity backpack upon check-in, and features menu choices prepared especially for young travelers. Parents are provided with a list of top family attractions in Dallas, local emergency numbers and a safety/first-aid kit which includes a night light and outlet covers.
Aloft Dallas Downtown1033 Young StreetDallas, Texas 75202 214/761-0000Rates: $-$$This super modern and hip boutique hotel from the Starwood brand boats brick walls, bright color accents and lots of window space, similar in feel to a SoHo loft apartment. It’s convenient to the Convention Center, downtown attractions and Business District, and takes advantage of the renaissance in arts and performance venues (and the restaurants that follow them) in the nearby Arts District. Comfortable double rooms have a living area with couch and work station, providing a good amount of space for the traveling family. The hotel also offers free WiFi, 24-hour minimarket, a state of the art exercise facility, outdoor pool, pet-friendly rooms, and a fun Re:mix Lounge with a pool table.
Hilton Anatole2201 Stemmons FreewayDallas, Texas  75207214/748-1200Rates: $-$$Plunk a big meetings center and 1,600+ room hotel in an eight-acre garden a few miles from downtown; then, add three swimming pools, racquetball courts and a world-class art collection with its own audio walking tour, and you have Trammell Crow’s signature Anatole. This long-popular Dallas landmark does holidays, weddings and family events in equally big measure, as you can see in this account of Christmas break at the Anatole. Because of its size and business-orientation, however, there are terrific bargains available on weekends and facilities to keep all ages busy.
Rosewood Crescent Hotel400 Crescent Ct.Dallas, Texas 75201214/871-3200Rates: $$$-$$$$A very posh hotel modeled after the Royal Crescent in England is almost reminiscent of a manor house in the clubby, dark wood style of its furnishings. The Rosewood Crescent Hotel near the Oak Lawn neighborhood has nearly 200 rooms — among them 29 one and two-story suites with up to two bedrooms, some with kitchens — located above a very high-end, air-conditioned shopping mall that is perfect for taking the little ones out in the stroller. Guests have access to The Crescent Club, an exclusive private dining club and bar on the 17th floor of an adjoining office tower with great city views. (It’s also known for the leather dance floor open weekend evenings when a live band performs.) The hotel offers lavish service and amenities, a pool, cribs, and babysitting services upon request, and some very fine dining on the premises, including a branch of the world-famous Nobu.
### Dallas Hotels in Other Neighborhoods
Le Meridien Dallas, The Stoneleigh2927 Maple Ave.Dallas, Texas 75201214/871-7111Rates: $$-$$$$This 11-story art deco hotel, a 1923 landmark, is more posh, polished and business-oriented since it joined Starwood’s le Meridien brand. Its location in Uptown has long attracted celebrity and long-term guests who are pampered with twice-daily maid service, the proximity of Dallas’ top bars and restaurants, and its pet-welcoming attitude. The hotel also has the new farm-to-table Graze restaurant with a varied kids’ menu, 24/7 business services, fitness center and a laundry.
Mansion on Turtle Creek2821 Turtle Creek Blvd.Dallas, Texas 75219214/559-2100Rates: $$$-$$$$Situated just north of the downtown area, this very plush, converted 1926 mansion offers its guests country quiet in the middle of the bustling city. Considered Dallas’ finest hotel because of its exceptional service, the beautifully restored hotel contains 143 spacious rooms, some with hand-carved fireplaces, wooden floors, and stained glass windows. It’s decorated throughout with European antiquities and some of the art bought abroad by its original cotton baron owners, who took their family on a Grand Tour of the Continent. Guests can enjoy a nationally acclaimed restaurant, health club, pool, cribs with fancy linens. It’s the perfect place to stay if the grandparents are hosting your clan to a Big D vacation or if you’re planning a traditionally romantic getaway.
### Planning a night on the town in Dallas?
All of the above hotels are affiliated with Dallas area babysitting services. They provide you with the phone numbers in order to allow you to select which service to entrust the care of your children.  One of the most highly accredited babysitting services used by area hotels is Babysitters of Dallas (214/692-1354), who’ve worked in this city since 1955. They are state licensed and bonded. Call before arrival and you can even book some babysitters to interview.
For general information on the Dallas, Texas area, contact the Dallas Convention & Visitors Bureau at 800/C-DALLAS or 214/571-1000.

Dallas, Texas Attractions for Families
Take a Family-Friendly Vacation to Dallas - The Big "D"Whether you’re a fan of Cowboys & Indians or the Dallas Cowboys, you’ll have fun with the family in Dallas.  And since they do everything big in Texas, there’s way too much to see on just one trip to the state’s largest city.  That’s why we’re sharing our top picks among Dallas attractions and activities;  most are open daily except for major holidays.
### Great Fun for the Kids
(Toddler to Age 8)

Perot Museum of Science and Nature2201 N. Field StreetDallas, TX 75202214/428-5555Although once separate entities, the Dallas Children’s Museum, Science Place and the Dallas Museum of Natural History have joined forces at this location. Many exhibits in the Perot will delight preschoolers but the Moody Family Children’s Museum takes this task to heart, with special interactive play areas designed for ages 5 and under, and casual seating for parents and minders. The museum offers free parent-child activities such as the Arts Lab, digging for dinosaurs, and an indoor nature hike. Drop-off Discovery day camps are designed for ages 3-5 and focus on sciences, arts and crafts.
Klyde Warren Park2012 Woodall Rodgers FreewayDallas, TX 75201Named for the son of the principal donor, this 5.2-acre urban space covers the recessed Woodall Rodgers Freeway between Pearl and St. Paul streets in downtown Dallas. It is now a public park with fountains, yoga classes, concerts, seating areas and our favorite — an outdoor reading room. Shelves are stocked with kids books that park visitors can leaf through when they’re done climbing, strolling, sunning or dining at a food truck. If you’re in the Arts District, make time to stop by and enjoy successful urban planning. Open daily 6am to 11pm.
Dallas Firefighters Museum3801 Parry Avenue (across from Fair Park)Dallas, TX 75226214/821-1500This little, old-fashioned museum constructed from a vintage fire station features rare firefighting memorabilia that will appeal to little firefighters. Keep in mind that the museum is closed from Sunday to Tuesday.
Dallas Puppet TheaterEntertaining tots and their parents for over 30 years, this delightful little puppet theater has lost its long-time home in Fair Park. Until they get resettled, visit their site to find free preformances at local area libraries and schools. The talented performers most often reenact classic versions of popular children’s fairy tales such as Cinderella and Little Red Riding Hood, making their shows appropriate for all preschoolers.
### Fun for Older Children
(Up to Age 18)
Dallas World Aquarium1801 North Griffin StreetDallas, TX 75202214/720-2224This aquarium and environmental learning center displays flora and fauna from five continents, 14 countries, three oceans, numerous seas and rivers. The excellent exhibits of marine wildlife add up to much more than your average aquarium. Special added attractions include the 400,000-gallon “Mundo Maya” tank that resembles an actual Mayan cenote (underground spring) and the South American rain forest exhibit featuring plant life and wildlife indigenous to the largest river in Venezuela. Take your family into the heart of the jungle to observe a tree boa, crocodiles, a three-toed sloth and a waxy monkey frog. Chilldren 2 and under free.
The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Gardens8525 Garland RoadDallas, TX 75218214/515-6515These beautiful gardens, with many shaded benches designed for leisurely visitors or weary grandparents, include 66 acres of lush flora, fountains, sculpture, and a historic mansion with restaurant. The Rory Meyers Children’s Adventure Garden is an 8-acre “museum without walls” that aims to set the gold standard in life, earth and environmental science education.  Children of all ages can learn about nature and concepts such as photosynthesis, pollination and the solar system in a highly interactive, age-appropriate and just plain fun manner. Engaging features include a 240-foot Texas Treetop Skywalk, Puppet Theatre in the Glade and The Amazon’s Secret Garden. Rainy Day passes are issued in case there’s actually inclement weather during your visit, and admission is free to children ages 2 and under.
Dallas Heritage Village1515 South HarwoodDallas, TX 75215214/421-5141Not far from downtown Dallas in Old City Park, dating from 1840-1910 and set on 13 acres, is this collection of restored homes and historic businesses. A great Living History destination, kids can visit a doctor’s office, railroad depot and farm. Guided tours are available once daily (audio guides are always there) except Monday when the area is closed to the public; the museum is also closed all of January and August.
### Fun for the Whole Family
The Sixth Floor Museum411 Elm Street (at Dealey Plaza)Dallas, TX 75202214/747-6660Grandparents and some parents will remember the Texas Book Repository as the spot where Lee Harvey Oswald lay in waiting to shoot President John F. Kennedy when his motorcade drove through downtown Dallas. At the time of the 50th anniversary of the Kennedy Assasination in 1963, it has evolved from a private collection of conspiracy theorists (some are still around) into a fascinating, multimedia look at 1960’s America, with a chronological display of news clips, amateur photographs taken by the crowd and, most interestingly, the many home movies taken at the time of his killing. Part thriller, part history, all intriguing to teens and adults; this small museum is well worth a visit.
Dallas Cowboys AT&T Stadium1 AT&T WayArlington, Texas 76011817/892-4161The hottest thing in town — even before the 2011 Super Bowl play — is Cowboys AT&T Stadium, a state-of-the-art indoor sports facility that leaves fans with their heads spinning. Families line up for the VIP Tours led by guides who will wow your football fans with their facts and figures. The enormous video scoreboard screen, over 150 feet, is enough to thrill even the football-hater. On the 90-minute VIP Tour, you will see private and media boxes, the Cotton Bowl offices, the field, several clubs, the post-game interview room and both the Cowboys’ and Cheerleaders’ locker rooms. Self-guided tours also available but limited schedules work around game times, so be sure to book ahead.
Dallas Museum of Art 1717 North HarwoodDallas, TX 75201214/922-1200A visit to the heart of the Arts District provides a chance to see the city’s ultra-modern skyscrapers up close. DMA features more than 17,000 works of art from around the world, as well as excellent ethnic and folk art galleries. In the main galleries, Arturo, the museum mascot, and any of the many weekly family activities make this a fun outing. The whole family can also visit the Center for Creative Connections (C3), where there are special touch, feel and explore sections designed to introduce art to all ages. Closed on Mondays; the museum has late Thursday sessions, and has started offering a free general admission policy (fees for special exhibitions may apply).
Childrens Aquarium at Fair Park Dallas1462 First Avenue (Fair Park)Dallas, TX 75226469/554-7340Here’s a great reason to visit Fair Park, the Art Deco-era Texas state fair grounds whose iconic Big Tex, a larger-than-life cowboy who greets all comers. Once a traditional, fish-in-a-tank aquarium, this newly renovated marineland is the largest in the Southwest and a partner with the Dallas Zoo. It boasts a collection of 3,500 specimens representing more than 320 different species of aquatic life. Exhibits include 6 unique zones including a Freshwater Zone, and Offshore Zone and Stingray Bay, as well as some unique creature such as an albino alligator, snapping turtle, upside down jellyfish and a 5-foot-long electric eel. For a dazzling feeding frenzy, call ahead for the shark and piranha feeding schedule. If the kids have limited interest, check out the smaller downtown World Aquarium (noted above).
For more general information, contact the Dallas Convention & Visitor Bureau at 800/232-5527 or 214/571-1000.  For information about other attractions in the Greater Metroplex region, read about Ft. Worth Family Attractions, the Mesquite Rodeo and the Arlington Texas attractions.

The sold out conference features a dynamic list of workshops aimed at improving the quality of writing and video production among family travels bloggers and reviewers.
This two-day conference has been organized by Eileen Ogintz, syndicated columnist and creator of Taking The Kids; Kyle McCarthy, creator of FamilyTravelForum.com; Kim Orlando, founder of TravelingMom.com and JoAnne Vero, who produces Travel Media Showcase every year.  A select group of A-list family travel bloggers and writers will participate in workshops on how they can hone their craft in this 21st Century media marketplace and discuss the latest family travel trends.
Family travel now accounts for well over 100 million trips a year and is one of the fastest growing segments of the leisure travel market with hotels, cruise lines, even adventure companies offering an ever growing array of programs and amenities for families. More than a million children now cruise each year; Baby Boomer grandparents increasingly are part of the equation. No parent or grandparent any longer apologizes for bringing a child, even to the toniest hotel.  On the contrary, today’s family travelers expect the travel industry to cater to them and their children.
The conference builds on the success of the inaugural FTC event in New York last February.  In a review of that conference on Technorati, Kaleel Sakakeeny, wrote: “Used to be they were called ‘mommy bloggers,’ but that was before their Klout scores soared and corporations avidly courted them. And while I may be exaggerating, I’m not by much. This group of bright, engaged mothers (and some dads) who travel with their kids and run homes and blogs, now run the family travel market and drive some of the most exciting conversations on line."
"We are thrilled that Dallas was selected to host the Family Travel Writers Conference," said Phillip Jones, President/CEO of the Dallas Convention and Visitors Bureau. "This top tier of family travel influencers will be some of the first to experience the brand new, state-of-the-art venues and attractions that Dallas offers thanks to our $15billion in new developments in the downtown area."
Today, scores of writers and bloggers are turning their attention to family travel as the travel industry works to please increasingly sophisticated young travelers with everything from junior gourmet menus to cooking  and language lessons to multi-million dollar kids’ and teen clubs. Despite this economy, families still put a high priority on vacationing together.
FTC Workshops will focus on a variety of subjects, including video editing, use of social media and monetizing brands. FTC Speakers include Genevieve Shaw Brown of ABCnews.com; Wendy Perrin, director of Conde Nast’s Consumer News and Digital Community, and many other industry leaders.

Hilton Anatole is a Big Dallas Hotel with Big Family Fun Activities
The Hilton Anatole Hotel is a big Dallas convention center hotel whose many facilities, fun events schedule and bargain, off-peak pricing make it a great value for families.
To put numbers to “big” we can say there are 1,606 hotel rooms and suites; 346,000 square-feet of meeting space including seven ballrooms; three swimming pools; tennis, racquetball and squash courts in an eight-acre garden; more than 1,000 pieces of art; and much, much more.
More than 80% of guests come to work. In its many years at the heart of Dallas commerce, the Anatole has hosted more conventions, business meetings and local incentives than any other venue in town. Guests who come to play enjoy huge weddings, celebratory events, fine dining and big entertainment. We really found a million twinkling lights, free concerts in the lobby and visits from local celebrities at our Christmas visit.
The Hilton Anatole has a big personality, too. Decor throughout the vast beige stone property ranges from multi-tonne slabs of the Berlin Wall, to lifesize carved wood elephants, Ming vases worthy of owner Trammell Crow (a big Asian art collector) and contemporary sculpture in the eight-acre garden.
A portrait of the late President Reagan astride a horse, next to a Frederick Remington style Western sculpture mounted outside the 25th floor Ronald Reagan suite, says it all.
### Room for the Whole Family and Then Some
As you can see from the video (see page 2), rooms are spacious and have an Asian flair and original artwork that place them a big cut above most convention hotel rooms. In addition to the 760 double rooms located in the hotel or The Tower, there are many king-bedded rooms that connect to them as well as 130 suites, most with pullout sofabeds.  In-room amenities include a pod coffeemaker, large workdesk with two-line phones, wired and WiFi access (HiltonHonors members get free WiFi access, a big plus for families too), and lots of room to spread out. We found the staff pleasant and helpful throughout.
Three executive floors in The Tower share a pleasant lounge on the 25th floor, where a small selection of continental breakfast items and afternoon tea, plus some snacks, are complimentary throughout the day. Upgrading to this level is a great value for families who want to hang out together because it gives you a comfortable lounge as well. At our holiday visit, it wasn’t uncommon to find children in PJs having breakfast or playing board games there.

### Christmas at the Anatole Activities and Attractions
Free to anyone passing through are the many Christmas trees, wreathes and winter tableaux. At our family’s 2013 visit (read the account here), we sang along with Rudolph and his anamatronic reindeer friends prancing in their stalls, visited Santa’s workshop where elves were busy at work, and posed for photos under the tallest nutcracker in Texas.
For a nominal fee, the annual “Sparkle” festival provides extra activities at the hotel that will keep everyone busy, and on cold days many musical events are brought indoors to the meeting spaces. During the late November to early January holiday period, families can count on outdoor “Movie Mondays,” a big game on “Football Sundays,” a Candyland Bounce House, large skating rink with rental gear and free lessons provided by celebrity skaters, origami workshops, a marionette puppet theater, visits from animal trainers and their wards from the Dallas Zoo and many other activities. On certain dates, dogs are welcome to romp in the outdoor gardens and Santa hosts breakfast for photo ops.
### More Family Activities All Year at the Hilton Anatole
There’s always free access to the Verandah Health Club, where there’s a great big pool that kids will love plus workout facilities galore — including squash courts — for those over age 16.
Allow enough time to take the hotel’s fun 1-mile ArtWalk. Yes, there’s an audio track you can stream from www.AnatoleArt.com that takes just 27 minutes, and while the kids get their bearings at the large white marble Buddha or the Jade Entrance filled with remarkable jade sculptures, the lively narration keeps everyone moving around the hotel, indoors and out. It’s a great way to get a fascinating glimpse of Trammell Crow’s magnificent art collection, which you can supplement at the small and wonderful Trammell Crow Museum of Asian Art nearby in the Dallas Arts District.
### Dining is a Big Dallas Event
The Hilton Anatole has a very good sports bar, the Media Grill, for burgers and salads, plus a pleasant Starbucks outlet if you want to have a light breakfast or lunch. But you’ll want to get out because Dallas has blossomed into a real foodie scene, perhaps driven by the many New Orleans families who emigrated here after Hurricane Katrina. Whatever the inspiration, the bubbling economy is keeping a wide variety of places at all price points busy.
We love the authentic local Mexican joints all over town for a quick midday burrito break. For something hipper, there are several branches of Torchy Tacos where you can get some great Tex-Mex at only $2.50 per taco plate and customize the toppings.
At night, it’s a very short drive over to the fun Bishop Arts District for nuevo Mexicano at Veracruz, or superb Italian at Lucia, among this neighborhood’s trendy and excellent international cuisine restaurants.
### Trip Planning Details for a Hilton Anatole Getaway
The Hilton Anatole Hotel (214/748-1200) is located at 2201 Stemmons Freeway, Dallas, TX  75207, just off I-35.  While the views reinforced the notion that we were in the middle of an industrial “nowhere” – in fact, the Hilton Anatole is located only 3 miles from downtown Dallas.
Here, Klyde Warren Park, the Perot Science Center and the art museums are among the major Dallas family attractions. It’s also close to the American Airlines Arena if you’re lucky enough to have Dallas Stars (hockey) or Dallas Mavericks (basketball) tickets.
Finally, the hotel is only 10 minutes from our favorite Love Field Airport, perfect if you’re flying Southwest Airlines. But if this is a big stop on your road trip, never fear. Parking is included in the Hilton Anatole room packages.
And the parking lot is big.

Texas Packs Dallas Holiday At The Arboretum In A Must-See Christmas Wonder
When winter arrives in Texas, the Dallas Arboretum transforms into a magical holiday destination that captures hearts across the state.
Families from near and far flock to this 66-acre botanical garden to witness one of the most spectacular Christmas displays in the entire country.
Located along the beautiful shores of White Rock Lake, this seasonal wonderland combines natural beauty with festive creativity in ways that leave visitors absolutely speechless.
From towering light displays to charming village scenes crafted entirely from natural materials, every corner of the garden sparkles with holiday magic.
Whether you are planning your first visit or returning for another year of wonder, these ten remarkable features will show you exactly why this Texas treasure has become a must-see Christmas tradition for thousands of families each season.

## The Spectacular 12 Days of Christmas Display
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
Each of the twelve days comes to life through massive, beautifully crafted displays that tower above pathways and nestle among winter blooms.
Partridges perch in carefully decorated pear trees while golden rings shimmer under twinkling lights.
Drummers drumming and pipers piping appear in whimsical interpretations that blend artistry with nature.
The level of detail in each display is truly remarkable, with artists spending months planning and constructing these seasonal masterpieces.
Children race from one scene to the next, counting along and singing the familiar song as they discover each new tableau.
Photographers find endless opportunities to capture magical moments, especially as twilight settles and the displays begin to glow.
The combination of traditional holiday imagery with the natural backdrop of the Texas gardens creates something genuinely unique.
Families often return multiple times each season because new details reveal themselves with every visit.
The displays remain stunning throughout the entire holiday season, maintaining their beauty from opening day through the final evening.
This signature attraction at 8525 Garland Rd, Dallas, TX 75218 has become the centerpiece of countless family traditions and holiday memories across the state.
## The Enchanting Christmas Village Walkthrough
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
Imagine strolling through a miniature European village where every building glows with holiday warmth and charm.
The Christmas Village at the Arboretum recreates this fairy tale experience with incredible attention to authentic details.
Tiny cottages line cobblestone style pathways, each one decorated with wreaths, garlands, and twinkling lights that reflect the spirit of old world holiday celebrations.
Visitors can peek into windows to see miniature scenes of holiday life, from cozy fireplaces to tiny decorated trees.
The village layout encourages leisurely exploration, with benches positioned perfectly for resting while soaking in the festive atmosphere.
Many families bring their cameras to capture children posing beside the charming structures, creating photo opportunities that look straight out of a storybook.
The garden setting adds natural beauty that indoor displays simply cannot match.
Staff members have thoughtfully placed the village to take advantage of existing trees and plants, creating seamless integration between constructed elements and living landscape.
Evening visits reveal the village at its most magical, when lights create a warm glow against the darkening Texas sky.
## Stunning Seasonal Flower Displays and Winter Blooms
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
Most people assume botanical gardens close or look barren during winter months, but the Dallas Arboretum proves this assumption completely wrong.
Horticulturists work year-round to ensure the gardens burst with color even during the coldest weeks.
Thousands of pansies, ornamental cabbages, and winter blooming flowers create vibrant carpets of purple, pink, white, and burgundy throughout the grounds.
These hardy plants thrive in cooler temperatures, offering spectacular color that rivals spring displays.
The Jonsson Color Garden becomes particularly breathtaking during the holiday season, with carefully planned arrangements that complement the Christmas decorations.
Gardeners select plant varieties that can withstand Texas winter weather while maintaining their brilliant hues.
Visitors often express surprise at seeing such lush, colorful gardens in December and January.
The combination of living flowers with holiday decorations creates a unique aesthetic that feels both festive and naturally beautiful.
Educational signs throughout the gardens identify plant varieties and offer tips for creating similar winter displays at home.
Families appreciate learning which flowers can brighten their own yards during the typically drab winter months.
The garden staff refreshes plantings regularly to ensure peak beauty throughout the entire holiday season, demonstrating the level of care and expertise that makes this Texas destination truly special.

© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
Standing at various viewpoints throughout the Arboretum, visitors can gaze across the sparkling waters of White Rock Lake, adding a serene natural element to the festive experience.
The lake serves as a stunning backdrop that changes throughout the day as light shifts across the water.
The peaceful water combined with garden beauty creates moments of tranquility that feel worlds away from busy holiday shopping and city stress.
Several benches and seating areas face the lake, providing perfect spots for quiet contemplation or family conversations.
Many visitors bring picnic blankets to spread on designated lawn areas where they can enjoy snacks while watching birds glide across the water.
The lakeside location also means pleasant breezes that keep the gardens comfortable even during sunny winter afternoons.
This natural climate control makes outdoor exploration enjoyable regardless of the weather.
Sunset visits become particularly memorable as the sky transforms into shades of pink and orange, reflecting off both the lake and the holiday displays.
The combination of natural beauty and festive decorations creates photo opportunities that feel truly magical.
Families appreciate having this natural element as part of their holiday experience, offering children space to explore nature while enjoying seasonal festivities at this beloved Texas destination.
## Family Friendly Kids Exploration Park and Play Areas
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
Parents know that keeping children engaged during garden visits can be challenging, but the Arboretum solves this beautifully with dedicated play spaces designed to blend fun with nature education.
The kids exploration park offers adventures that let young ones burn energy while learning about the natural world.
Interactive exhibits teach children about plant life cycles, local wildlife, and environmental stewardship through hands on activities.
Climbing structures mimic tree houses and natural forms, encouraging imaginative play that connects kids with nature.
During the holiday season, these areas receive festive touches that maintain the Christmas spirit while preserving their educational mission.
Children can participate in seasonal scavenger hunts that send them searching for specific decorations or natural elements throughout the gardens.
The play areas give parents a chance to rest on nearby benches while keeping children within easy view. This thoughtful design makes family visits more relaxing for everyone involved.
Many families plan to spend several hours at the Arboretum specifically because these play spaces mean children remain happy and engaged throughout the visit.
The combination of structured gardens and free play areas creates balanced experiences that appeal to all ages.
Staff members regularly update activities and seasonal programs, ensuring that return visitors always find something new to explore and enjoy at this exceptional Texas family destination.
## Gorgeous Holiday Lighting and Evening Illumination
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
As daylight fades, the entire Arboretum undergoes a magical transformation that rivals any theme park light display.
Thousands of carefully placed lights bring trees, pathways, and garden features to life in ways that feel both elegant and wonderfully festive.
Lights wrap around tree trunks and branches, creating glowing canopies overhead while leaving the garden structure visible and beautiful.
The lighting design team plans placement to guide visitors along pathways while highlighting specific garden features and holiday displays.
Color choices remain tasteful, with warm whites and traditional holiday hues that feel timeless rather than trendy.
Evening visits offer completely different experiences from daytime tours, making many families choose to visit twice during the season. The cooler evening temperatures also make walking more comfortable, especially during unseasonably warm Texas winter days.
Photographers particularly love the evening hours when lights create dramatic contrasts and warm glows perfect for capturing memorable images.
The combination of artificial lighting and natural twilight produces a brief window of absolutely perfect photographic conditions.
Special evening events sometimes feature live music or seasonal performances, adding another layer of entertainment to the visual spectacle.
These nighttime experiences have become highlights of the holiday season for countless Texas families.
## Peaceful Walking Trails and Garden Pathways
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
Beyond the major displays and attractions, the Arboretum offers miles of peaceful pathways that wind through diverse garden environments.
These trails provide opportunities for quiet reflection and gentle exercise while surrounded by beauty.
The Red Maple Rill features a long water feature that creates soothing sounds as visitors stroll alongside.
During the holiday season, this area receives tasteful decorations that enhance rather than distract from the natural water and plant features.
Shaded sections offer comfortable walking even during sunny afternoons, while open areas provide warming sunshine on cooler days.
The variety of environments means visitors can choose routes that match their comfort preferences and energy levels.
Clear signage helps guests navigate the extensive grounds without feeling lost or overwhelmed.
Maps available at the entrance show estimated walking times for various routes, helping families plan their visits effectively.
Many visitors appreciate that the garden layout accommodates both quick visits and extended explorations. You can see highlights in about two hours or spend an entire day discovering hidden corners and quiet spaces.
The pathways remain accessible for strollers and wheelchairs, ensuring that everyone can enjoy the gardens regardless of mobility considerations.
This inclusive design reflects the Arboretum’s commitment to welcoming all visitors to experience Texas natural beauty during the holiday season.
## Charming On Site Cafes and Dining Options
© Restaurant Degolyer
Exploring 66 acres of gardens works up quite an appetite, and fortunately the Arboretum provides convenient dining options right on the grounds.
Several cafes offer comfortable indoor and outdoor seating where visitors can refuel without leaving the garden.
Families appreciate having reliable meal choices available, eliminating the need to leave and return during extended visits.
The cafe locations provide pleasant views of garden areas, allowing diners to continue enjoying the scenery while resting tired feet.
Indoor seating offers climate-controlled comfort during particularly hot or cold days, while outdoor tables let guests dine surrounded by nature.
During the holiday season, cafes sometimes feature special seasonal menu items that add festive touches to the dining experience.
The convenience of on-site dining means more time enjoying the gardens and less time worrying about meal logistics.
Visitors frequently mention in reviews that having these dining options enhances their overall experience significantly.
The ability to take breaks for snacks or full meals makes all day visits comfortable and enjoyable for families with young children.
Prices remain reasonable considering the quality and convenience, with portion sizes that satisfy hungry visitors.
The cafes also accommodate visitors who bring their own food, with designated picnic areas available throughout the Texas gardens.
## Exceptional Staff and Welcoming Atmosphere
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
From the moment you arrive, the friendly staff at the Arboretum work to ensure every visitor feels welcomed and valued.
Team members stationed throughout the gardens offer assistance, answer questions, and share interesting facts about plants and displays.
Reviews consistently praise staff friendliness and helpfulness, noting how employees check in with guests to ensure positive experiences.
This level of personal attention feels increasingly rare at large attractions, making it especially appreciated here.
During busy holiday periods, staff members help direct traffic and manage crowds efficiently while maintaining warm, patient attitudes.
Their expertise about the gardens and local plant life adds educational value to visits, especially for families with curious children.
These details demonstrate the organization’s commitment to visitor comfort and satisfaction.
Many guests mention feeling genuinely cared for during their visits, which transforms a simple garden tour into a memorable experience.
The staff’s passion for the gardens and genuine desire to share that love with others shines through in every interaction.
This combination of beautiful surroundings and exceptional hospitality explains why so many families return year after year, making the Arboretum a cherished part of their Texas holiday traditions.
## Perfect Photo Opportunities Throughout the Grounds
© The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
Every turn reveals another picture perfect moment waiting to be captured, making the Arboretum a paradise for photography enthusiasts and families wanting holiday card photos.
The combination of natural beauty, artistic displays, and thoughtful design creates endless photographic possibilities.
Professional photographers often bring clients here for portrait sessions, taking advantage of the stunning backdrops and varied settings available within the gardens.
Families can achieve similar results with smartphone cameras thanks to the naturally beautiful lighting and colorful surroundings.
Popular photo spots include the Christmas Village, the 12 Days of Christmas displays, and lakeside viewpoints that offer both festive and natural elements.
Early morning and late afternoon provide the most flattering natural light for outdoor photography.
The gardens remain spacious enough that photographers can work without feeling crowded or rushed, even during busy weekend visits.
This breathing room allows everyone to capture the specific shots they envision without competing for position.
Many visitors create annual traditions of taking family photos at the same locations each year, documenting how children grow while the beloved gardens remain a constant backdrop.
These progressive photo series become treasured family keepsakes over time.
Social media fills with tagged photos from the Arboretum throughout the holiday season, spreading word about this Texas treasure and inspiring others to plan their own visits to this genuinely magical destination.

# 13 Iconic Dallas Attractions & Activities for Young Adults to Add to Your Itinerary
Jon Miksis
Updated January 22, 2026
Most Beautiful Destinations Around the World
by 										Jon Miksis
Updated: January 22, 2026
445
The moment I stepped into the Dallas Museum of Art and saw that massive Pollock up close, I knew this city was going to surprise me. Dallas isn’t just about cowboys and steakhouses (though trust me, you’ll want to hit up those steakhouses). Between the wild nightlife in Deep Ellum and the skyline views from Reunion Tower, this city has an energy that caught me completely off guard.
After exploring the best things to do in Dallas, from catching a Stars game at American Airlines Center to roaming through the mind-blowing art collections at the DMA, I’ve put together my 13 favorite spots. Whether you’re into world-class art, killer food, or just vibing in one of America’s most underrated cities, these places will show you why Dallas deserves your attention.
## Top Sights to See in Dallas for Young Adults
Looking for the coolest things to do in Dallas for young adults? Take in stunning city views from Reunion Tower GeO-Deck, enjoy a night of laughs at Dallas Comedy Club, get your adrenaline pumping at Zero Gravity Thrill Amusement Park, and explore world-class exhibits at the Dallas Museum of Art.
Dallas is big, so I mapped out my favorite spots for young adults below. Save this map to your phone to easily explore culture, nightlife, and local eats.
### 1. Explore the Skyline at Reunion Tower GeO-Deck
Start your Dallas trip with a panoramic view from the Reunion Tower GeO-Deck, one of the city’s most iconic landmarks. At 470 feet high, the indoor and outdoor observation decks give you a 360-degree look at the skyline, neighborhoods, and even planes flying into Love Field. It’s especially great at sunset when the city lights start to glow. I went just before dark and stayed long enough to see the shift—it was a cool way to see Dallas transform.
Touchscreens on the deck offer info about key landmarks you’re looking at, and there’s a café upstairs for drinks with a view. Whether it’s your first time in the city or you’ve been here before, it’s a simple way to get your bearings and snap a few photos. Don’t skip the telescopes—they’re free to use and fun for spotting landmarks.
- Going at sunset? This Reunion Tower GeO-Deck ticket includes the interactive screens and free telescopes.
A visit to Reunion Tower is consistently enchanting, offering an ideal introduction to Dallas and a unique city perspective.
### 2. Dive into the Comedy Scene at Dallas Comedy Club
Dallas Comedy Club in Deep Ellum is a great pick for a casual night out with friends. The vibe here is laid-back and unpretentious, with a solid mix of improv, stand-up, and sketch comedy. You never know what you’re going to get, and that’s part of the fun. I went on a Friday and ended up catching a local showcase that had the whole room cracking up.
If you’re feeling brave, there’s open mic night, and yes, the crowd is actually supportive. The venue has a full bar and small bites, so you can keep the laughs going without leaving your seat. Shows tend to fill up quickly on weekends, so I’d suggest booking ahead. Whether you’re into sharp one-liners or chaotic improv games, this is an easy way to spend an evening full of laughs in Dallas.
The atmosphere at Dallas Comedy Club strikes the perfect balance – coziness and buzzing energy. | Image Credits: Dallas Comedy Club
### 3. Catch Thrills at Zero Gravity Thrill Amusement Park
Adrenaline junkies, Zero Gravity Thrill Amusement Park is calling your name. This compact park is all about high-intensity experiences—none of the kiddie rides, just straight-up thrills. I tried the Texas Blastoff, and getting launched skyward at 70 mph is something I won’t forget anytime soon.
There are five extreme rides, including Nothin’ but Net, where you free-fall 130 feet without a harness into a giant net. It’s wild. The park is easy to navigate, and they offer combo packages if you want to do more than one ride. Staff are great about explaining the safety measures, which helped calm my nerves before the drop. If you’re in Dallas with a group of friends and want something a little out of the ordinary, this is the spot for an intense afternoon or night of fun.
Take your Dallas adventure to new heights at Zero Gravity Thrill Amusement Park, a paradise for thrill-seekers.
### 4. Uncover Artistic Wonders at the Dallas Museum of Art
You don’t have to be an art expert to appreciate the Dallas Museum of Art. Located in the Dallas Arts District, it’s free to enter and surprisingly massive, with over 24,000 works spanning thousands of years. One of my favorite finds was Jackson Pollock’s Cathedral—it’s even more intense in person than in photos.
Whether you’re escaping the Texas heat or just want to do something more low-key, this place is worth the visit. Bonus: the museum café makes a solid coffee if you need a recharge.
The DMA consistently features diverse traveling exhibitions, ensuring a continual influx of new and captivating displays.
### 5. Savor Flavors at Lower Greenville
Lower Greenville is one of Dallas’ go-to neighborhoods for food and nightlife. With its mix of trendy restaurants, casual joints, and rooftop bars, it’s a solid pick for young adults looking to eat well and hang out. The vibe feels effortlessly cool, especially when the patios fill up on weekend evenings.
I grabbed dinner at Wabi House—their pork belly buns were legit—and followed it up with drinks at HG Sply Co., where the rooftop view adds to the atmosphere. Whether you’re craving ramen, tacos, or vegan eats, there’s something for every taste.

Lower Greenville comes alive in the evenings, creating an ideal atmosphere for dinner and drinks.
### 6. Score Big at Bishop Cidercade’s Arcade and Cider Bar
Bishop Cidercade is the ultimate hangout for gamers and cider lovers. Located in the Design District, it offers unlimited arcade play for just $12. You can jump from classic pinball and Donkey Kong to newer rhythm and racing games, all without needing tokens. I spent hours trying to beat my friend’s Skee-Ball score—and failed, but had a blast doing it.
Bishop Cidercade in Dallas is family-friendly by day and transitions into a 21+ venue after 8 PM for nighttime fun.
### 7. Relax and Play at Klyde Warren Park
Right in the heart of downtown, Klyde Warren Park is a surprisingly lively green space built over a freeway. It’s great for tossing a frisbee, catching a food truck lunch, or just laying back on the lawn with a book. I stopped by on a Sunday afternoon and ended up joining a free Zumba class near the stage area.
The park has something for everyone—live concerts, yoga sessions, ping-pong tables, and a rotating line-up of food trucks. The Reading and Games Room is stocked with board games and books you can borrow, which makes it ideal for chill afternoons with friends. It’s also dog-friendly and filled with locals, which gives it a very laid-back feel.
Whether you’re passing through or planning to stay a while, Klyde Warren is one of those spots that helps you slow down and enjoy Dallas.
Klyde Warren Park transcends being a mere park; it serves as a community hub, breathing life into the best of Dallas.
### 8. Enjoy Movies with Gourmet Flair at Alamo Drafthouse Cinema
It’s perfect for film lovers who appreciate the details. Whether you’re with friends or on a casual date, the mix of comfort food and curated cinema makes Alamo Drafthouse one of the coolest entertainment spots for young adults in Dallas.
Experience a redefined movie outing at Alamo Drafthouse Cinema, where a perfect fusion of film, food, and drinks awaits.
### 9. Explore and Experience the Dallas Arts District
The Dallas Arts District is the city’s cultural hub, packed with iconic venues and creative energy. Spanning 68 acres, this walkable neighborhood includes the Winspear Opera House, Nasher Sculpture Center, and Dallas Museum of Art, all within a few blocks. I started at the DMA and ended the day listening to live jazz on the Sammons Park lawn—laid-back and inspiring all at once.
The Dallas Arts District stands as a dynamic neighborhood, a cultural playground where art, music, and theater seamlessly converge.
### 10. Unwind at White Rock Lake
If you need a break from downtown Dallas, White Rock Lake is the perfect escape. Locals love it for jogging, biking, kayaking, or simply relaxing by the water. The setting is calm and scenic, with wide-open views and a peaceful vibe you wouldn’t expect this close to the city.
The 9.3-mile trail loops around the lake and makes for a solid workout or casual stroll. You’ll pass fishing piers, shaded picnic spots, and great photo ops—especially at sunrise or sunset. There are no rental shops on-site, so bring your own gear if you’re paddling or biking.
Nearby, the Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden is worth checking out if you want to extend your day outdoors. Whether you’re catching a breeze by the shore or stretching your legs, White Rock Lake is one of those spots that hits the reset button without leaving Dallas.
For adults seeking enjoyment, White Rock Lake stands out as a haven for outdoor enthusiasts in Dallas.
### 11. Groove at Deep Ellum’s Live Music Venues
I caught a local funk group at Ruins, and it turned into one of those random, unforgettable nights where everything just clicks—cheap drinks, good company, and a crowd that’s really into the music. Even if you’re not into live shows, the area’s art-filled alleys and dive bars are worth exploring.
Some venues allow under-21 guests earlier in the evening, so check listings. Whether you’re dancing by the stage or bar-hopping with friends, Deep Ellum always delivers the energy.
Discover diverse musical experiences in Deep Ellum by exploring various venues that showcase a wide range of music genres.
### 12. Skate and Socialize at Galleria Dallas Ice Skating Center
Right in the middle of a massive shopping mall, the Galleria Dallas Ice Skating Center is a surprisingly fun break from browsing stores. Whether you’re pulling off spins or just trying to stay upright, skating here is a blast. I tagged along with friends one afternoon, and even with my lack of coordination, we couldn’t stop laughing.
Enjoying a skate at Galleria Dallas ranks among the most delightful activities for young adults in Dallas.
### 13. Embark on a Historic Journey at The Sixth Floor Museum
For a deeper look into American history, visit The Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza, housed inside the former Texas School Book Depository. The exhibits trace the life, presidency, and legacy of John F. Kennedy, culminating in the events of November 22, 1963. It’s a thought-provoking experience that offers both context and emotional weight.
Walking through the space where history unfolded felt surreal. The window corner where the sniper allegedly stood is preserved exactly as it was. The multimedia displays and personal accounts provide insight beyond textbooks. Plan to spend at least an hour or two exploring the exhibits.
Afterward, take time to walk around Dealey Plaza and reflect on the spot that forever changed the country’s narrative. For young adults interested in politics or history, this museum leaves a lasting impression.
- For more context beyond the exhibits, this JFK assassination and Sixth Floor Museum tour covers Dealey Plaza and Oswald’s rooming house.
Exploring The Sixth Floor Museum offers a profound experience for young adults visiting Dallas.
Discover an array of enjoyable activities for young adults in Dallas, whether it’s history, arts, or socializing.

These 12 spots completely changed my mind about DFW.

Looking for places to live in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex? Explore Allen, a thriving city with top-rated schools and family-friendly amenities. Outdoor enthusiasts will love Celebration Park, a 96-acre hotspot featuring sports fields, a splash pad, and scenic walking trails. Shopping and dining thrive at Watters Creek at Montgomery Farm, an open-air lifestyle center with boutique shops, restaurants, and live music events. For bargain hunters, Allen Premium Outlets delivers major brand discounts.
Beyond its low crime rate and strong job market, Allen’s prime location off US-75 ensures easy access to Dallas, Plano, and McKinney. Whether you’re raising a family or seeking a thriving community, Allen offers top-tier amenities, a welcoming atmosphere, and unbeatable convenience—a true standout in the Metroplex.

Carrollton’s food scene is incredible, featuring everything from authentic Korean BBQ in Koreatown to Tex-Mex favorites. The charming Downtown Carrollton Square hosts community events, local boutiques, and cozy cafés, adding a small-town touch to this bustling suburb.
For outdoor enthusiasts, Elm Fork Nature Preserve provides lush hiking trails and scenic escapes. Families benefit from top-rated schools in Carrollton-Farmers Branch ISD, while professionals enjoy a booming job market in technology, healthcare, and logistics. With affordable housing, a strong economy, and a vibrant community, Carrollton offers big-city perks with a friendly, suburban feel, making it a top choice for families and young professionals.

Families are drawn to Grapevine-Colleyville ISD, one of the top school districts in Texas, while professionals appreciate the short commute to DFW Airport. Andrew Brown Park provides a scenic escape with walking trails, playgrounds, and sports fields, while the Coppell Aquatic and Recreation Center is a favorite for active residents.

Irving is also a cultural hotspot, boasting The Mustangs of Las Colinas, the world’s largest equestrian sculpture, and the Toyota Music Factory, a live music venue that hosts major concerts and events. Foodies can explore everything from authentic Tex-Mex to international cuisine, reflecting the city’s rich multicultural vibe.
With easy access to DFW Airport, Irving is perfect for frequent travelers and business professionals. The city’s affordable housing, strong job market, and vibrant nightlife make it one of the best places in the Metroplex for young professionals, families, and those looking for an energetic, well-connected community.
Irving is the greatest place to live in the DFW Metroplex since it provides a wide range of experiences.
### 9. Keller
Keller delivers small-town charm with all the perks of a thriving, upscale suburb. Known for its top-rated Keller ISD schools, spacious homes, and family-friendly atmosphere, it’s a go-to destination for those seeking quality of life without sacrificing convenience.
Keller is a hidden suburban treasure that provides a peaceful way of life without sacrificing contemporary conveniences.
### 10. Plano
The city’s schools, part of Plano ISD, consistently rank among the best in Texas. Parks and nature lovers will appreciate Arbor Hills Nature Preserve, offering hiking trails, scenic views, and biking paths. Legacy West and The Shops at Legacy create an upscale live-work-play environment, filled with high-end shopping, trendy restaurants, and buzzing nightlife.
With low crime, exceptional schools, and a robust job market, Plano offers the perfect blend of urban convenience and suburban comfort. Whether you’re a young professional or a growing family, this highly livable city has something for everyone.
Plano is a dominant city with a thriving community and robust economy.
### 11. Richardson
Although it is a tech-savvy city, Richardson hasn’t forgotten its history.
### 12. University Park
For those who value education, elegance, and a serene lifestyle, University Park is one of DFW’s most desirable places to live. Home to Southern Methodist University (SMU), this affluent neighborhood exudes a refined yet welcoming atmosphere, blending academic prestige with upscale living.
Tree-lined streets and luxurious homes define University Park, but it’s not just about real estate—it’s about quality of life. Snider Plaza is the heartbeat of the community, offering upscale boutiques, charming cafés, and fine dining. Nearby, the Meadows Museum houses one of the largest Spanish art collections outside of Spain, adding a cultural touch.
Families flock to top-tier Highland Park ISD schools, while professionals enjoy a short commute to downtown Dallas. With its pristine parks, cultural institutions, and tight-knit community, University Park is a picture-perfect neighborhood for those seeking sophistication, safety, and top-tier amenities.
University Park is a quiet neighborhood with peaceful surroundings.
There is something for everyone in the Dallas Metroplex.

# Guide to Dallas with Teens: Six Flags, Deep Ellum & BBQs

Updated January 6, 2026
Most Beautiful Destinations Around the World
by 										Jon Miksis
Updated: January 6, 2026
656
Dallas is a city that knows how to keep things fresh, fun, and full of energy. Whether it’s the electric vibes of Deep Ellum, the high-speed thrills of Six Flags, or the hidden gems tucked away in vibrant neighborhoods, Dallas offers a mix of experiences that are perfect for teens. Picture this: cruising through the coolest skate parks, grabbing gourmet tacos from food trucks, or exploring quirky art installations that spark creativity at every turn. As someone who’s spent time in the city, I can tell you that Dallas is a place that’ll excite both you and your teens. It’s bold, adventurous, and full of surprises. Let’s dive into 15 awesome things to do with teens in The Big D!
## Best Things to Do With Teens in Dallas
Exploring Dallas for teens is an adventure filled with diverse activities that cater to all interests. From thrilling amusement parks to cultural museums, our guide covers the top spots that teenagers will love.
I know Dallas is huge, so I mapped out all my favorite teen-friendly spots below. Save this map to your phone so you can easily bounce between museums, theme parks, food stops, and outdoor hangouts.
### 1. Ride rollercoasters at Six Flags Over Texas
If your teen craves heart-pounding excitement, Six Flags Over Texas is the ultimate adrenaline rush. This massive amusement park is packed with roller coasters, thrill rides, and water attractions, making it a full-day adventure. The Titan, one of the tallest and fastest coasters in Texas, will have you soaring at 85 mph, while Mr. Freeze: Reverse Blast catapults riders backward at lightning speed. The first time I rode The New Texas Giant, I thought I had prepared myself—until the steep drop had me gripping the safety bar for dear life.

For those who love a splash, the Aquaman: Power Wave is a hybrid coaster and water ride that delivers a refreshing jolt on hot days. If you plan to visit, grab a Flash Pass to skip long lines, and don’t forget to refuel with a classic funnel cake—because no trip to Six Flags is complete without one.
Experience the thrill at Six Flags Over Texas is the ultimate destination for exhilarating rides and family fun.
### 2. Zip line through the trees at Trinity Forest Adventure Park
Credit: Viator
This is self-guided once you’re trained up, meaning teens can tackle courses at their own pace and push themselves as much as they want. The whole setup feels more adventurous than typical ropes courses because you’re actually in a forest.
Book a morning slot before it gets blazing hot, and bring water bottles since there’s limited shade. Gloves are required but not included, so bring your own or buy them there for ten bucks.
### 3. Explore the Perot Museum of Nature and Science
For a hands-on, mind-expanding experience, the Perot Museum of Nature and Science is a must-visit for teens who love to explore. This multi-floor museum brings science to life with interactive exhibits, from racing a virtual T. rex to experiencing an earthquake simulation. The T. Boone Pickens Life Then and Now Hall showcases towering dinosaur skeletons, while the Expanding Universe Hall offers a deep dive into space exploration. I still remember stepping onto the motion-capture sports science exhibit, convinced I had a decent vertical jump—until the data proved otherwise.
Discover the Perot Museum is an engaging science hub offering interactive experiences.
### 4. Hang out at Klyde Warren Park
Right in the heart of downtown Dallas, Klyde Warren Park is a green oasis where teens can unwind, people-watch, or dive into a variety of activities. The park’s open space is lined with food trucks serving everything from gourmet tacos to Thai-style ice cream rolls, making it a great place to grab a bite and relax. On weekends, the lawn buzzes with yoga sessions, live music, and pickup games of frisbee or soccer. One time, I ended up joining a free salsa class here on a whim—it was way more fun than I expected, even if my footwork was questionable.
The park also has a game area with oversized chess boards and ping-pong tables, plus a reading room stocked with books and magazines. Whether you want to lounge under the trees or take part in a spontaneous dance lesson, there’s always something happening here.
Klyde Warren Park is an urban oasis, a hotspot for young adults seeking relaxation and fun amidst lush greenery.
### 5. Eat BBQ and Tex-Mex on a Deep Ellum food tour
Deep Ellum’s food scene hits different, and this three-hour tour takes you straight to the best stuff. You’re sampling BBQ brisket from Pecan Lodge, Texas chili con carne, Tex-Mex quesadillas, bourbon pecan pie, and a mystery Secret Dish that changes based on what’s best that day. Between food stops, you’re walking through streets packed with murals and learning how this former industrial area became Dallas’s creative hub.
Credit: Getyourguide
Deep Ellum stays lively after the tour ends, so stick around if your teens want to explore the record shops and street art. The whole neighborhood is walkable from the meeting point on Main Street.

### 6. Hit golf balls at TopGolf Dallas
For a competitive yet laid-back outing, TopGolf Dallas is a great spot where teens can test their swing without the seriousness of a traditional golf course. This high-tech driving range turns golf into a social game, with microchipped balls tracking your shots and scoring every hit. Whether you’re aiming for the farthest targets or just happy to make solid contact, it’s a fun way to spend an evening with friends. The first time I played, I went in thinking it would be easy—but after a few embarrassing swings and laughs, I finally nailed a long shot that felt incredibly satisfying.
Beyond golf, the venue has pool tables, shuffleboard, and a solid menu of burgers and loaded fries, making it a full-on hangout spot. Visit on a weekday afternoon to avoid long waits, and don’t be surprised if your teen asks to come back for a rematch.
TopGolf in Dallas: modern golf fun for teens with interactive targets and high-tech swing feedback.
### 7. Check out the Museum of Illusions
The museum is a photographer’s dream, so make sure your phone is charged for creative snapshots. Since it’s a popular attraction, booking tickets online ahead of time helps avoid long waits. Whether you’re laughing at impossible illusions or trying to crack a puzzle, this place keeps you engaged from start to finish.
The Museum of Illusions captivates illusions and interactive installations for teens and young adults.
### 8. Have a picnic with downtown Dallas skyline views
Credit: Airbnb
The location at Bridge Dallas delivers legitimately stunning skyline views, especially during sunset bookings. Everything was so well put together, it actually felt special, not just another activity.
Reserve an evening slot for the best light and cooler temps. Trinity Groves is just a five-minute drive away if you want dinner afterward with more skyline views.
### 9. Tour the Dallas Cowboys stadium
Depending on the tour, you might even get to visit the press box or VIP areas usually reserved for players and celebrities. To get the full experience, opt for a self-guided tour so you can explore at your own pace. It’s a rare glimpse behind the scenes of one of the NFL’s most iconic franchises.
- Skip the hassle: This AT&T Stadium tour with transportation includes pickup from downtown Dallas.
Experience the Dallas Cowboys Stadium Tour, an immersive journey into the heart of American football.
### 10. Feed giraffes at the Dallas Zoo
For an up-close wildlife experience, the Dallas Zoo offers more than just a walk through animal exhibits—it’s a place where teens can get hands-on and interactive. The zoo’s Wilds of Africa section is a standout, featuring a monorail safari ride that glides over open habitats filled with elephants, giraffes, and hippos. The Giants of the Savanna exhibit is one of the few in the country where giraffes and elephants share space, creating a more natural environment. Feeding the giraffes here was unexpectedly fun—I didn’t expect their tongues to be that long!
If your teen is into conservation, check out the behind-the-scenes Keeper Chats, where zookeepers share stories about the animals and their care. The zoo is large, so comfortable shoes are a must, and if you visit in summer, arriving early helps beat the Texas heat. It’s a classic yet engaging way to spend the day.
- Save money: The Dallas CityPASS includes zoo admission plus three other top attractions.
Discover the Dallas Zoo, a vibrant, teen-friendly destination showcasing diverse animals.
### 11. Watch a Texas Rangers game at Globe Life Park
For teens who love sports, catching a Texas Rangers game at Globe Life Park is an unforgettable experience. The energy of a live baseball game—fans cheering, the crack of the bat, and the scent of ballpark snacks—is something that’s hard to replicate anywhere else. Even if baseball isn’t your teen’s top sport, the stadium’s modern design and interactive elements make it fun for everyone. My first time here, I barely paid attention to the innings because I was too busy hunting down the best ballpark nachos (which, for the record, were worth it).
Credit: @danielp220 on TripAdvisor
Arrive early to explore the park, grab a photo with the Rangers’ mascot, or catch batting practice. Tickets are often affordable, especially for weeknight games, making this a great budget-friendly outing. Whether you’re a die-hard fan or just soaking in the atmosphere, a night at the ballpark is a Dallas classic.
Catch a Texas Rangers game at Globe Life Park and immerse in the vibrant atmosphere.
### 12. Kayak or bike around White Rock Lake
For a break from the city’s fast pace, White Rock Lake Park offers a peaceful escape with plenty of space to explore. Teens who love the outdoors can rent a kayak, go biking along the scenic trails, or just relax by the water. The park’s 9-mile loop is a favorite for runners and cyclists, and the sunset views from the lake’s edge are some of the best in Dallas. One time, I tried stand-up paddleboarding here and quickly learned that balance is not my strong suit—I spent more time in the water than on the board.
The Dallas Arboretum is nearby, so you can combine a visit to both for a full day of outdoor fun. If you’re planning a picnic, there are plenty of shaded spots, and weekends often bring live music and community events. It’s an underrated gem that locals love for good reason.
White Rock Lake Park is a haven for outdoor enthusiasts and nature lovers.
### 13. Ride the mini-train at Dallas Zoo
At the Dallas Zoo, the Conservation Railway Mini-Train is more than just a ride—it’s a charming way to see the park from a different perspective. This all-electric train loops around Picnic Ridge, offering a relaxing break from walking while giving riders a fun view of different animal exhibits. With animal-themed designs and playful sound effects, it’s a nostalgic ride that appeals to visitors of all ages. The first time I rode it, I figured it was just for little kids, but I ended up enjoying the scenic ride and unique vantage points more than expected.
Credit: @Old-Socialist on TripAdvisor
The train is a great option if your teen needs a break from walking, and it’s especially nice on hot days when you need a bit of shade and a breeze. Tickets are separate from zoo admission, so plan ahead if you want to add this to your visit.
Ride the Conservation Railway Mini-Train at Dallas Zoo: a fun, animal-themed experience for teens and families.
### 14. Visit the Dallas Arboretum
The Dallas Arboretum isn’t just for plant lovers—it’s a surprisingly fun and relaxing spot for teens who appreciate nature, photography, or just a peaceful place to unwind. Spread across 66 acres, the gardens change with the seasons, featuring vibrant tulip displays in spring and massive pumpkin patches in fall. The infinity pool overlooking White Rock Lake is a perfect photo spot, and the Rory Meyers Children’s Adventure Garden has interactive exhibits that explain plant science in a hands-on way. I wasn’t expecting to enjoy the edible garden so much, but sampling fresh herbs straight from the plants was surprisingly cool.
If you visit in summer, arrive early to avoid the heat, and check their event calendar—outdoor concerts and night-time garden walks make the experience even more special. Whether your teen is a nature enthusiast or just looking for a scenic escape, the arboretum is a hidden gem.
- A private Dallas Arboretum tour covers all 66 acres with a guide who knows the best photo spots.
Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden is a serene oasis, perfect for teens to enjoy nature’s beauty and tranquility.
### 15. Learn about JFK at the Sixth Floor Museum
For history buffs and curious minds, the Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza offers an insightful look into one of the most significant moments in American history. Located in the former Texas School Book Depository, the museum tells the story of JFK’s presidency, assassination, and lasting legacy. The exhibits include historical photos, artifacts, and even the window from where the fatal shots were fired. Walking through the timeline of that day felt surreal—it’s one thing to read about history, but standing in the actual location makes it hit differently.
The museum also provides context on the political climate of the 1960s, making it an educational experience beyond just the assassination. Tickets can sell out, so booking in advance is a good idea. Whether or not you’re a history buff, it’s a powerful visit that leaves a lasting impression.
- After the museum, this JFK trolley tour follows the motorcade route to Dealey Plaza and beyond.
The Sixth Floor Museum showcases insight into JFK’s life, assassination, and legacy, ideal for history-minded teens.

I’ve discovered the best things to do in Dallas at night by diving into every corner of Big D after dark. From epic nights in Deep Ellum’s live music scene to stunning skyline views at Reunion Tower, these spots prove Dallas nights are anything but ordinary. Get ready for some serious Texas-sized fun!
- 👉 Pro Tip: I HIGHLY recommend this haunted bar crawl through downtown Dallas! They take you to four historic pubs where guides share spine-chilling ghost stories and local legends. ## 19 Things To Do At Night In Dallas
Dallas at night is a world of its own, brimming with excitement and charm. Dive into our guide to discover where to visit in Dallas at night, from dazzling entertainment to tranquil escapes!
### 1. Explore downtown Dallas on an electric bike tour
- This Dallas night e-scooter tour covers Deep Ellum and the Arts District in two hours.
Explore Dallas on an electric bike—an unconventional and exciting way to discover the city’s attractions.
### 2. Sip cocktails at Dallas’ best rooftop bars
HIDE on Lowest Greenville is hands down one of the coolest rooftop spots you’ll find in Dallas. This place has been killing it since moving from Deep Ellum – they’ve got over 30 signature cocktails and honestly, their pizza is way better than you’d expect from a cocktail bar. The rooftop patio gives you solid downtown views, and I actually love that it doesn’t feel too fancy or pretentious.
Most places open around 3-5pm and stay open until midnight or later on weekends. Expect to spend $12-18 per cocktail, but happy hours usually run until 6pm with better prices. I’d definitely make reservations for weekend nights – these spots get packed, especially when the weather’s nice.
### 3. Get panoramic city views from Reunion Tower GeO-Deck
One of the most iconic landmarks of Dallas is the Reunion Tower. Standing tall, it’s hard to miss this structure when you’re in the city. But the real magic? It’s at the top, on the GeO-Deck.
The GeO-Deck offers a bird’s-eye view of Dallas. Current admission runs $19-40 for adults depending on the time, with discounts for seniors ($16-35) and kids ($10-20). As you step onto it, the city stretches out below, a sea of lights and life. I was amazed by how different everything looks from 470 feet up – you can see for miles on a clear day. The interactive touch screens tell you about the landmarks you’re looking at, so you’re not just seeing the city but learning about it too.
Time your visit for sunset if possible. The Day + Night ticket ($24-40) lets you experience both the golden hour and the sparkling city lights. Pro tip: parking is $10 for up to four hours, so plan accordingly.
- Skip the ticket line: This Reunion Tower GeO-Deck admission gets you straight to the 360-degree views.
The unforgettable sight of the city transitioning from day to night from the GeO-Deck is a mesmerizing experience.
### 4. Laugh until your sides hurt at Dallas comedy clubs
Dallas Comedy Club in Deep Ellum is where you want to go for the real deal. They’ve got something happening almost every night – from improv shows to stand-up to storytelling events. Friday and Saturday “Primetime” shows are their biggest draws, but honestly, I’ve had some of my best laughs at their free Wednesday night improv club shows. The venue’s intimate, so even bad seats are pretty good.
Hyena’s Comedy Nightclub at Mockingbird Station brings in national headliners regularly, and their two-item minimum isn’t as brutal as some places. Four Day Weekend has been doing improv in Dallas forever – they’re actually really good at getting the audience involved without making it awkward. Addison Improv is a bit of a drive but worth it for bigger names.
Most shows run $15-25 for general admission, more for special events. You’ll need to arrive 30 minutes early to keep your reservation, and yeah, there’s usually a two-drink minimum. Shows typically start at 7:30pm and 10pm on weekends. I always check who’s performing before booking – some comedians are definitely better than others.
